scenarios.text: + one directory's entries spread over all MDTs (name hash), finer MDT locks (done: ROCEPOOL_DIR_STRIPE=1 + MD_BUCKETS; a no-op on a run that already has them)
+ FOPEN_PARALLEL_DIRECT_WRITES: no per-node inode lock on a shared file

+ FUSE over io_uring (per-core queues, Linux 6.14+): ~3x per-mount rate, less wake-up cost (implemented: io500_run.py probes it against /dev/fuse on the hosts and uses the faster; a no-op on a run that already used it)

+ the LD_PRELOAD interception library in every rank (no FUSE channel, no kernel on the I/O path; implemented: io500_run.py --client auto probes it against FUSE and uses the faster; a no-op on a run that already used it)

+ one-sided reads and lookups (client RDMA READs stripes and MDT entries; implemented: io500_run.py --direct-read auto probes it; a no-op on a run that already used it -- its effect is in the measured per-op server CPU)

+ the OST's NVMe tier for the 300 s write phases (implemented: roce/native/ost_tier.c, io500_run.py --ost-tier auto; a no-op on a run that already had it -- its limits are then the drives' capacity and write bandwidth)
